parole.significato: An ephah, a former Hebrew unit of dry volume (about 23 L).
parole.testo: From Egyptian jpt (“oipe, a dry measure of volume about 19.2 liters”); compare Sahidic Coptic ⲟⲉⲓⲡⲉ (oeipe).

parole.significato: papyrus (a plant (Cyperus papyrus) in the sedge family, native to the Nile river valley, paper reed)
parole.testo: Uncertain, possibilities include: * From גָּמָא (gāmā, “to sip, to swallow”), with the sense of "the plant that swallows water" (according to Gesenius). * From Egyptian ḏmꜥ (“roll of papyrus, book of papyrus”), compare with Bohairic Coptic ϫⲱⲙ (jōm) and Sahidic Coptic ϫⲱⲱⲙⲉ (jōōme).

In modern Hebrew from the Bible, where it is a hapax. Probably borrowed from Egyptian hbnj, itself of uncertain origin (possibly from Nubian). Cognate with Ancient Greek ἔβενος (ébenos) and all its derivatives, including ebony and أبنوس.

Borrowed from Egyptian ḏrt (“hand”). Compare Classical Syriac ܙܪܬܐ (zartå, “span; hand”), Ugaritic 𐎏𐎗𐎚 (ḏrt), Classical Mandaic ࡆࡉࡓࡕࡀ (zirta). In the sense of "span", attested in the Tanakh; in the sense "pinky, little finger", attested since the Mishnaic Hebrew period.
Borrowed from Egyptian ḫpš.

parole.significato: ring (a circumscribing object, (roughly) circular and hollow, looking like an annual ring, earring, finger ring etc)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian ḏbꜥwt (“signet”).

parole.significato: A river, stream, or canal, especially in Egypt, especially the Nile.

The word was borrowed into Hebrew after the shift of Egyptian /t/ to /ʔ/, which is attested from the 18th Dynasty onward in the form of the alternative spelling jrw. From Egyptian ʿrq, later rq. Compare Ugaritic lg.

Hoffmeister suggests מ־ (ma-) + Egyptian ḫt (“fire”). Klein and Even-Shoshan derive מַ־ (instrumental prefix) + חָתָה (“to rake or snatch coals from a hearth with fire-tongs”) + ־ָה.

Following the former it is derived from the root כָּנַס (kanás, “to cover, hide”), as the purpose of the priestly undergarments was to further hide the intimate parts (see Exodus 28:42 below).
